svg.title: How a 16-point FFT splits its input into bit-reversed order
svg.desc: Five rows show a 16-sample signal being split. Row 1: one signal of 16 points, samples 0 to 15. Row 2: two signals of 8 points, the even samples 0 2 4 6 8 10 12 14 and the odd samples 1 3 5 7 9 11 13 15. Row 3: four signals of 4 points. Row 4: eight signals of 2 points. Row 5: sixteen single points in the order 0 8 4 12 2 10 6 14 1 9 5 13 3 11 7 15. Each position holds the sample whose 4-bit index is the position written backwards, for example position 1 = 0001 holds sample 1000 = 8. Adapted from Burnett-Thompson (2007).
svg.text: Splitting 16 samples into even and odd, four times over
Bit reversal: write the position in 4-bit binary, read it backwards, and that is the sample that lands there.
